page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is an arm64-based server instance powered by the Neoverse-V2 CPU architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing 64 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. It supports AES cryptography but lacks AVX, AVX512, and AMX extensions. This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance rated as strong and passmark CPU physics testing reaching top-tier levels. Memory performance is highly competitive, showing top-tier results in read-only small block cached bandwidth and large block write bandwidth. In application-specific workloads, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and PassMark database operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also top tier, while single-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU encryption tests fall into the average category.

The c4a-highcpu-64 offers high resource density for compute-bound workloads, delivering strong multi-threaded efficiency and memory bandwidth. However, the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators limits its utility for tasks requiring high-speed local disk I/O or heavy graphics processing. The 2.0 GB per core memory allocation represents a tradeoff, prioritizing raw compute power over memory-intensive caching. This profile is highly suitable for high-throughput web serving, database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
